title:
Comment of Frances L YatesMarch in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152106.txt
documents.text:
Frances L YatesMarch, Anchorage, AK.
Commercial Fishing in Alaska is a billion dollar business. “Alaska fishermen harvest an average of 5.1 billion pounds of seafood annually, bringing in $1.5 billion paid directly to fishermen at the docks. Once seafood processors finish and package the raw catch into finished goods the total wholesale value rises to $4.2 billion.The industry accounts for roughly $1.9 billion in direct annual labor wages and multiplier effects, distributed across more than 41,800 workers and fishermen.” This is taken from National Fisheries data. Putting in a data center in Cook Inlet endangers fishing. I have read the impact of placing a data center in the ocean raises the waters by 1 degree celsius or more. Rising temperatures in the ocean effects species migration, starvation for species that feed off the marine life in that area, fueling of storms impacted by the heat exchange of warmer waters, and ocean deoxygenation that feeds of carbon emissions. This proposal will impact Alaska’s economy, and our climate as a whole. 

Cook Inlet has some of the most extreme tidal dynamics in the world because of bore tides. I have read that this will cause structural fatigue on moorings and frames. Also, the Cook Inlet is known for it’s massive amount of silt. This silt is abrasive and will make maintenance on The data center difficult if not impossible. It is difficult to fathom how this structure will remain sound. 

I am also concerned about the noise level the data centers cause. The humming causes continuous noice and vibrations that will effect wildlife and people who live in the areas surrounding Cook Inlet. 

The Deep Green Industry is located in London, England. If they want a data center let them build it there, or not at all. Please do not build this monstrosity in the Cook Inlet.
